In restoring an Instagram video of a woman describing her experience with prescription fentanyl during childbirth, the Oversight Board recommends Meta take steps to ensure correct enforcement of existing medical exceptions to policies covering illicit drugs, and further protection of the free expression rights around sharing pregnancy and maternal health information.
Why This Matters
Social media is a vital source of pregnancy and maternal health information globally for people seeking guidance and peer support, including sharing their experiences with prescription drugs. Overenforcement of Meta’s community standards on drug-related maternal health content is a widely documented problem that suppresses well-intentioned personal storytelling and maternal health advocacy. At the same time, there has been a worldwide proliferation of drug use and trafficking. In the United States, where this case originates, there is an opioid crisis. Illicit fentanyl use is the primary driver of overdose deaths in the country, and moderating content related to illegal drugs is a serious concern for platforms.
About the Case
In February 2026, an Instagram user posted a 20-second video and caption describing the side effects she experienced from several types of prescription drugs used to treat nausea and vomiting during her pregnancy. She also described her experience with pain relief medication, including fentanyl, which was clinically administered during labor. In the post, she said that fentanyl is “on my permanent no list” because the drug made her confused. The video features imagery with memes and short, humorous movie clips representing how each medication affected her during her pregnancy.

In analyzing the spread of AI-generated content in armed conflicts in a case on the 2025 Israel-Iran war, the Oversight Board calls on Meta to do more to allow users to identify such output. Its approach to surfacing AI-generated content must evolve. This includes providing details at scale about the origin of media, based on
content provenance standards
, investing in stronger detection tools and developing better methods for appropriate labeling. Meta needs to create a new, separate set of rules to ensure users can reliably recognize AI-generated content. Additionally, it should amend its current policies to ensure a timely and adequate response to deceptive AI-generated output.
The company needs to meet its public commitments and employ its own tools and others available across the industry to effectively address deceptive generative AI content that spreads among platforms.

In a case involving a Russian activist who attempted to burn but then tore up his passport at a press event, the Oversight Board finds that Meta should carve out an exception to its privacy policies governing personally identifiable information (PII) to permit individuals to publicly disclose their own PII as an act of political expression.
Why This Matters
Meta’s privacy policies have understandably strict prohibitions on the posting of PII, even well-intentioned self-disclosure, to protect all users from the heightened risks of physical and financial harm from disclosing PII in the public domain. However, a newsworthiness allowance can also be applied for posts that have a high public interest value. This case has important implications for how political speech is governed and how users are protected on Meta’s platforms.
About the Case
In August 2025, a leading German news agency shared an image on its Facebook page of an individual’s torn Russian passport. The biodata page was visible in the post, revealing the individual’s PII. A caption in Russian accompanied the post, stating that the passport owner is a dual German and Russian citizen, who was previously convicted of treason in Russia for taking a picture of a military unit close to where he had been living. The passport owner was released from prison as part of a prisoner swap and is now based in Germany.
The news agency’s Facebook post was part of its coverage of a press event where the passport owner first attempted to burn the passport, then tore it and threw it on the ground, reportedly saying: “I am ashamed of Russia. I do not want to be a citizen of Russia, which tortures so many people.”
